title: Sasanian Mesopotamia
subtitle: 224–637 AD · The Heart of Ērānšahr — Ctesiphon the Imperial Capital, the Nahrawan and the Richest Land on Earth, the Church of the East and the Talmud, and the Arab Conquest

categories.label: Power
categories.subtitle: Ardashir making the Sawad the empire's core, Shapur I and the captured Roman emperors, Shapur II's long war, the fifth-century disasters, Kavad and Mazdak, Khosrow I's great reforms, Khosrow II's last war, and the Arab conquest

categories.label: Conflict
categories.subtitle: Shapur's three triumphs over Rome and the fall of Hatra, the Roman counterstroke and the peace of 298, Julian's death before Ctesiphon, the sack of Antioch, Heraclius in the Sawad, and al-Qadisiyya and the fall of the capital

categories.label: Order
categories.subtitle: The Sawad as the heart of Ērānšahr and its richest tax base, Ctesiphon the greatest city of the West, Khosrow I's cadastral tax reform, the Zoroastrian state and the four estates, the protected communities under their own heads, and the marzbans and dihqans

categories.label: Belief
categories.subtitle: The Church of the East organised under a catholicos at Seleucia-Ctesiphon, the academies of Sura and Pumbedita and the redaction of the Talmud, Zoroastrianism as the state church, Mazdak's revolt, Mani, and the Mandaeans and the pagan survivals

categories.label: Expression
categories.subtitle: Syriac literature and the schools of Nisibis and Edessa, the Talmud as a literary monument, Sasanian rock relief and silver, the Book of Kings compiled at court, and the great vault of Ctesiphon

categories.label: Thought
categories.subtitle: Gondeshapur and its medicine, the translation movement under Khosrow I gathering Greek and Indian learning, the dialectic of the rabbinic academies, Syriac Aristotelian scholarship, and the royal astronomical tables

categories.label: Economy
categories.subtitle: The Nahrawan and the Sawad's agriculture at its historic peak, the richest tax base in the world, the silk trade and the Gulf ports, the cities peopled with Roman deportees, and the fire-altar drachm

categories.label: Technology
categories.subtitle: The pitched-brick vault of the Taq Kasra, the engineering of the three-hundred-kilometre Nahrawan, the norias of Hit and the piedmont qanats, and the pontoon bridges and the posting road

categories.label: Exchange
categories.subtitle: The three-century war with Byzantium over the same ground, the Church of the East reaching India and China, al-Hira and the Lakhmid buffer, the Jewish world centred on Babylonia, and the Sasanian apparatus passing whole to Islam

categories.label: World
categories.subtitle: Mesopotamia the heart of a great power again for the first time since Hammurabi, the plural society of three institutionalised communities, the two exhausted empires when the Arabs came, and early Islamic Iraq as Sasanian Iraq renamed

categories.label: Lives
categories.subtitle: The catholicos of the East at the royal city, the head of the academy at Sura or Pumbedita, the dihqan of the village, the deported Antiochene craftsman, and the court physician of Gondeshapur
